newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen mired after ceding ground on trade worry.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen mired after ceding ground on trade worry.

text.p: The dollar was little changed after falling from Wednesday's 11-week highs against the yen as comments by a Japanese auto industry official fanned concern that trade tensions between the U.S. and Japan could resurface.
Traders were also unwilling to add to their dollar holdings before the release of the second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product report later on Thursday and the July jobs report on Friday.
"Trade will always be a focus for the market as long as Japan is running a current account surplus with the U.S.," said Jesper Dannesboe, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London.
Also, "it would be premature to buy dollars at these relatively high levels before we get the data out of the U.S."
Dollar/yen, which rose as high as 118.95 on Wednesday, was at 117.63/73 yen at 0747 GMT from 118.15/25 late yesterday in Europe.
The dollar was at 1.8320/30 marks from 1.8337/47 yesterday. It was at 1.5094/04 Swiss francs, down from yesterday's 47-month high of 1.5261 and 1.5137/47 at the European close.
Takao Tominaga, the vice chairman and executive managing director of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association, said 110 to 120 yen was an appropriate range for the dollar.
He added that he did not want dollar/yen to be stronger than its current levels because of the implications for trade.

The dollar has surged as much as 60 percent from the post-World-War-II low it set in April 1995, eroding U.S. exporters' competitiveness against their Japanese rivals and the value of their yen earnings.

While the dollar has fallen back nearly 7 percent from the 57-month high of 127.46 yen it hit on May 1, U.S. exporters are still dissatisfied. Andrew Card, president of the American Automobile Manufacturers Association, said U.S-Japan automotive relations were deteriorating, Jiji Press reported yesterday.
